verdict.root_cause: Checkout errors visible at frontend originate on the checkoutservice -> cartservice edge. Every failing PlaceOrder trace aborts at checkoutservice's outbound client span for CartService/GetCart, which carries an error status that propagates up through checkoutservice, frontend's PlaceOrder and the frontend HTTP root [tr_f6db098f108b]. Those failing calls produce no cartservice server-side span and end in 2-4ms, indicating an immediate connection-level rejection rather than a slow dependency [tr_f6db098f108b]. checkoutservice is only the reporter: its self-time in failing traces is ~0.1-0.2ms, it keeps accepting orders at a steady cadence, and it logs no errors, timeouts or resource limits [tr_73a8955b0079, tr_f6db098f108b]. No dispatch examined cartservice itself, so the mechanism behind the refusal (crash/restart, listener or pool limit, wrong endpoint, bad artifact) is not established by this evidence.
verdict.reasoning: The traces are the only dispatch with a peer dimension and they localise the error origin to the GetCart client span, with the ERROR status inherited upward - which explains frontend, loadgenerator and checkoutservice all alerting from one fault [tr_f6db098f108b, tr_37bb607ee689, tr_f0db5295bd36]. It also explains the log shape: order-start lines continue while payment, email and publish lines disappear, because execution never passes cart [tr_73a8955b0079]. Payment, email, currency, shipping and catalog hops succeed in healthy traces and are never reached in failing ones, and checkoutservice's own change log is empty [tr_f6db098f108b, tr_dd2c91695fac]. paymentservice's empty metric series predates the incident and is an instrumentation gap, not a signal [tr_802990ccc0e7]. Sub-4ms failures with no server span exclude dependency_latency, and nothing on the board evidences a wrong artifact or a wrong config value, so the failing mechanism stays unknown; restarting/replacing cartservice replicas is the best first action, not a diagnosis.
open_questions: cartservice was never dispatched: its metrics, logs, restart/OOM counts and change history are wholly unexamined, and the mechanism lives there.
Why GetCart produces no cartservice server span - process gone, connections refused at a limit, or endpoint misresolved.

Frontend's error ratio crossed threshold at 08:31, before the cart failure onset bracketed at ~08:41:50-08:46:06, so an earlier or second contributor is unaccounted for [tr_37bb607ee689, tr_f6db098f108b].

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice pods were killed or throttled after exhausting memory or connection capacity, refusing GetCart RPCs while restarting.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible given instant refusals with no server span, but no cartservice memory, restart or saturation metric was ever queried, so exhaustion is inferred rather than observed [tr_f6db098f108b].

alternatives.root_cause: A configuration value on cartservice or its cart backend names a wrong address, port or credential, so connections are refused at once.
alternatives.why_not: No change history was queried for cartservice, and healthy GetCart with a working HGET child earlier in the same window shows the path was correct minutes before, which a static wrong value would not allow [tr_f6db098f108b].

alternatives.root_cause: An unrelated earlier fault raised frontend errors from 08:31 and the cart failure is a second, later problem.
alternatives.why_not: The frontend error-ratio query has no peer dimension and cannot attribute the 08:31 rise to anything; every sampled failing trace resolves to the cart edge [tr_37bb607ee689, tr_f6db098f108b].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any metric should be expected. The blocking observation is that cartservice has never been dispatched: the only evidence touching it is second-hand, from checkoutservice's outbound client spans [tr_f6db098f108b]. A restart of cartservice would be expected to show failing GetCart client spans stop carrying error status and checkoutservice's error ratio return toward its flat-zero baseline within a couple of minutes - but that prediction cannot be responsibly made until cartservice's own restart count, OOM count, log stream and change history are read, because the same trace signature (no server span, 2-4ms immediate rejection) is produced by process-gone, listener/pool exhaustion, and a misresolved endpoint alike, and only the first of those is fixed by a restart.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a dispatch against cartservice returns a restart or OOM-kill count rising inside the 08:41:50-08:46:06 onset bracket [tr_f6db098f108b], or a log stream that ends abruptly at onset - that would meet restart_service's precondition (process state, not change) and make restart_service on cartservice the right proposal. It is also wrong in the opposite direction if cartservice change history shows a config or image change inside the window, in which case revert_config or rollback_image is indicated and a restart would have recreated the same broken process. Note that restarting cartservice now would itself destroy the in-process and log evidence needed to tell these apart, so the cost of acting early is not only a possible no-op.
proposal.risk: The risk being avoided: if the refusal is caused by a configuration or endpoint change rather than process state, restart_service recreates the container with the same bad configuration, produces no recovery, and consumes the one cheap diagnostic window - while still dropping every in-flight GetCart and discarding cartservice's in-process cache. If the mechanism is instead an upstream or shared-infrastructure fault (cartservice's own dependency), a restart masks onset timing without fixing anything. The residual risk of abstaining is that checkout stays broken for the minutes a cartservice dispatch takes; frontend is at ~5% mean error ratio with ~30% peaks [tr_37bb607ee689], so this is partial degradation, not a total outage, and the delay is affordable.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing is being changed. For reference, the action deferred here would have touched cartservice alone; its inbound callers are frontend and checkoutservice, both already erroring, and frontend's cart-page reads would have seen resets during the recreate on top of the current PlaceOrder failures. A second, unexplained contributor is also unaccounted for: frontend's error ratio crossed threshold at 08:31, well before the cart onset bracket [tr_37bb607ee689, tr_f6db098f108b], so any cartservice action may leave part of the frontend error ratio in place and should not be judged solely on frontend recovery. checkoutservice itself is excluded as a target: its self-time in failing traces is ~0.1-0.2ms, it keeps accepting orders at a steady cadence and logs no errors [tr_73a8955b0079, tr_f6db098f108b] - it is the reporter, not the source.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend and checkoutservice within seconds of each other, plus the load generator, describe a user-facing checkout failure that cannot be dismissed. No open incident to attribute it to, and the alert pattern alone does not distinguish a bad deploy from a failing downstream dependency.
